steps.text: Preheat and lightly grease a large skillet or electric griddle.
Mix flour, salt, and baking soda together in a bowl. Add egg, buttermilk, and butter; stir together lightly, but keep it lumpy. The batter should look thick, spongy, and puffy.
Drop 1/3 cup of the batter onto the cooking surface, spreading lightly with the bottom of the cup. Cook until lightly browned on each side, 1 to 2 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom’s Buttermilk Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: The best buttermilk pancake mix to make light and fluffy pancakes. This favorite family recipe goes well with berry syrup — a special breakfast treat.

review.reviewBody: The first time I made these I followed the directions exactly and they were OUTSTANDING; light and fluffy as air. The second time I made them I did not have any buttermilk in house so I made some buttermilk using milk and vinegar. The second batch was good but nowhere near as good, or as light and fluffy as the first batch I made with the real buttermilk. I don't know why they weren't as fluffy but if I have any recommendations to make I would tell you to use the real buttermilk for the best results! Added fresh blueberries to the buttermilk batter and they were delicious that way as well! This is so very simple to mix together, that I will never use the packaged pancake mixes again. When I double this I double all the ingredients except for the salt. I just love making things from scratch for my family whenever I can and this is just as simple as a boxed mix, but much, much better!!!!! Update! I added a teaspoon of Vanilla Extract to the batter - took this recipe OVER THE TOP!

Cut back salt to 1/2 tsp, add 2 tsp vanilla and 1 cup of blueberries. Once complete, let the batter sit for about 10 minutes for fluffier results. As another reviewer mentioned, these need to be watched carefully. Awesome!

I substituted 1 cup whole milk with 2Tbsp of apple cider vinegar, and when the thickness of kefir, I added it to the dry ingredients. I forgot to put the butter and didn’t find the pancakes overly salty. The batter also spreads nicely. Will definitely be making these again!

These were delicious. I used non-iodized salt, and fresh butter and buttermilk. I made the butter/buttermilk in my stand mixer the night before and chilled the buttermilk overnight. The result was delicious - the pancakes were not heavy but had a slightly sweet and slightly savory flavor. With some fresh butter and real maple syrup, these pancakes disappeared quickly. Using a 1/4 cup measure to scoop out the batter and spread it around on the griddle think we got about 6 1/2 pancakes yield out of the ingredients listed in the recipe. Our pancakes were about 7" so that might explain why we came up short of the recipe's predicted yield, but I doubt you will get 12 pancakes like they predict.

Great pancakes BUT, use 1/2 Tsp. of salt, (half what the recipe calls for). Take butter off the heat as soon as it's barely melted. Mix dry ingredients in a canister with a lid by shaking it all together. Then add all the mixed/beaten wet stuff to the dry. First try was too salty but after adjusting the salt, they were awesome!

Good starter recipe. As mentioned elsewhere, much, much too salty and I am not overly sensitive to salt. (Absolutely did NOT overpour the salt!) Reducing salt by at least 1/2 and it was excellent. I also added a wee bit of sugar and vanilla.

Soo light and fluffy! (And yes, as written, too salty for most people.) I used 1/2t salt instead of the full t and I’m considering going down to 1/4 next time. I wouldn’t cut the baking soda at all. I also added a little coconut extract which I always do when making pancakes. Other extracts or citrus fruit zest would be great too but are not needed. These pancakes are delicious plain.! The batter is thick (light but thick) so they don’t form perfectly round pancakes but who cares. They also don't form the popped bubble top by the time the bottoms are done (which is usually how you know when to flip) so you need to watch them carefully. So yummy! I absolutely will make these again. And again and again. Lol
Cut salt in half, add 1tsp baking powder and 1 tsp vanilla extract - SUPERB!!!!!!

So stinkin good, so spongy and fluffy and I’m pretty sure I overmixed them. And I love the fact that it doesn’t make too many to the point where I’m standing at the griddle for 40 mins. It made 6 medium sized pancakes and 2 mini waffles(dash waffle maker). I did add two tablespoons of sugar since I didn’t see any and chocolate chips. I’ve made 5 different homemade recipes for pancakes and this will replace my last one that I thought was good.

Best pancakes ever!!!! This was my grandmother's recipe. It tastes exactly as I remembered as a child. I never had the chance to watch her make it from scratch. I made a few changes to it. I cut down the salt by half, I added 2 teaspoons of vanilla. To give it a sweet taste 1/3 cup of sugar. SO AMAZING!!!!!! MY family loves it.
Following the advice of other reviewers, I used only 1/4 teaspoon of salt and a scant teaspoon of baking soda. They came out great! The recipe as written makes four medium-to-large pancakes.
This is the recipe I use over and over for pancakes
I added a teaspoon of sugar. Next time I will decrease the salt a little.
Our recipe is similar but uses half the salt, half the soda, and adds 1tsp of baking powder. They’re perfect.
Some blue berrys and whip cream
Simple easy good.
Who in their right mind would think these are good? I think someone sabotaged the recipe. That was way to salty and not fluffy at all.
I added some vanilla and a dash of cinnamon
Made these twice, second time I cut the salt in half much better with less salt
Super simple recipe and a great way to use up sour milk!
